resolutions.researcher_notes: Current ref (sgc-oc.com PDF) re-verified: HTTP 200 (page is LIVE, not a dead link despite the DEAD_LINK class), but re-confirms the prior deep-sweep researcher's finding that it is the wrong document — verifier fails on token '800' (already full-text extracted by the prior pass: zero occurrence of 'Шуртан', 'Шерабад', or '800' in ~2,000 lines; it is SGC-OC's non-technical environmental summary for the unrelated Baysun GPZ/Surhan gas-field project). Ran a fresh Russian- and English-language search specifically hunting a diameter figure: 'Шуртан-Шерабад газопровод диаметр 800 мм', '"Шуртан-Шерабад" газопровод Ду800', '"Шуртан-Шерабад" 800 мм трубопровод', plus targeted fetches of mineral.ru, cabar.asia, gazeta.uz (2021), and maxsus.uz (Maxsusenergogaz, a trunk-gas-pipeline construction/reconstruction contractor whose site independently surfaced and which confirms the pipeline's SECOND line — 161 km + a 32 MW compressor station, under construction — but states no diameter for either line) and utg.uz/ru/about/history/ (404, page gone). No source anywhere states a diameter for this pipeline. Consistent with the prior researcher's exhaustive search (Russian- and English-language, Uztransgaz-adjacent material, technical literature) also finding nothing. 800mm remains uncited after two independent research passes; per standing rule 2, leaving UNRESOLVED rather than fabricating or reusing the mismatched PDF. Flagging for a possible future pass against a Uztransgaz internal asset register or Soviet-era VNIPItransgaz-style technical table, which is where comparable Uzbek/Kazakh trunk-pipeline diameters have surfaced elsewhere in this project — none located this pass.

Three independent Russian-language sources name both endpoints, Shurtan (Kashkadarya region, at/near the Shurtan gas field) and Sherabad (Surkhandarya region), both in Uzbekistan. mineral.ru, 2003-09-04 (Interfax wire via Uzbekneftegaz): 'магистрального газопровода Шуртан-Шерабад' running from Shurtan to Sherabad to supply southern Uzbekistan, bypassing Turkmenistan. neftegaz.ru technical entry on the Shurtan field: confirms Shurtan is a real, named gas-condensate field/settlement in Kashkadarya (Guzar district) region, Uzbekistan — the pipeline's start point. gazeta.uz, 2021-04-06 (unrelated Surkhandarya gas-financing story, independently reused here): 'Действующий магистральный газопровод «Шуртан-Шерабад»' (the existing/operating trunk gas pipeline Shurtan-Sherabad), confirming both place names and that the line runs through/toward Surkhandarya region 18 years after construction — a genuinely independent, later re-confirmation, not the same wire story. All three verified live with 'Шуртан'/'Шерабад' present in visible text. Reused from the deep-sweep audit shard's own Location [ref] fill (which additionally sourced province-level detail); this unit only needed the base StartLocation/EndLocation/CountryOrArea values, which all three sources support directly. Per source-roster policy, the ru.wikipedia Sherabad-district page the prior pass had provisionally included was NOT carried forward here (Wikipedia is never cited directly).
